content:
Phase 36 plan submitted: docs/phases/visual-story-portfolio-feed-30-arc.md (brief: docs/tagteam-3.0-proposal.md §4 Phase 36, §5 → ships as 3.0.0, §6). Branch phase-36-visual-story; PR at the end. Docs + media only — no package code, flags or schema; pyproject bump only.

Designed flow-first with the ux-design-guide skill (plan §"UX design"): three readers (GitHub visitor / portfolio visitor / showcase reader); diagnosis = README IA follows build order not reader intent, flat hierarchy, inconsistent terms; principles = mental models (reader's order: problem → loop → try it → one cycle → unattended → watch & steer → reference), progressive disclosure (depth → docs/how-tagteam-works.md, coverage ledger maps every current README paragraph to a destination), visual hierarchy (four mermaid diagrams ARE the outline), consistent language (glossary fixed up front).

Deliverables: (A) README restructured, 4 mermaid blocks; (B) docs/how-tagteam-works.md incl. "Files tagteam writes" table; (C) docs/media/: tagteam-loop.svg 800×260, tagteam-modes.svg 800×240 (Manual → Watched → Headless ladder = the honest analog of aegis-tiers), tagteam-cycle.svg, tagteam-headless.svg, three real 1280×800 screenshots, manifest with palette/conventions/regeneration recipe — verified against the actual aegis-*.svg in the portfolio repo (dark #1a2332 panels, teal/violet/green strokes, monospace, role=img + aria-label, no external refs, ≤20 KB); (D) docs/showcase.md for an outside reader; (E) scripts/showcase_numbers.py — stdlib, reads tracked docs/handoffs + .tagteam/legacy JSONL (dedupe, docs/handoffs wins), rounds-to-approval / actions / round-10 line, optional --usage snapshot for the headless token curve, so the showcase numbers are generated not typed (today's data: 30 cycles, 150 rounds, all approved, plan median 3 max 7, impl median 2 max 4, 26 headless turns); (F) tests/test_docs_story.py — SVG conventions, link/fence integrity, CLI-coverage (every cli.py command documented in README ∪ HTW), SVG↔mermaid label consistency, script arithmetic on a fixture + smoke over the repo, narrow glossary guard; (G) 3.0.0 bump, roadmap, findings.

Success criteria incl. `git diff v0.12.0 -- tagteam/` empty and `tagteam upgrade` no-op. Three open questions for you (PNG screenshots vs SVG mockups; keep/drop the glossary guard; one HTW file vs split).

The story, progressive-disclosure structure, coverage ledger, and docs-only boundary are strong. Please revise these blocking points before approval.

1. Make the evidence and screenshot pipeline public-safe and reproducible. The proposed committed `tagteam usage --json` snapshot is not safe as-is: the actual output contains absolute `log_path` values under `/Users/...`, session IDs, timestamps, model/agent metadata, and other fields the showcase does not need. Likewise, capturing the hub against the real 44-project registry can expose private project names, and cockpit screens may expose cycle text. Specify a minimal sanitized snapshot schema (only fields needed for the charts), a deterministic sanitizer/export command, and tests that reject absolute paths plus disallowed fields such as `log_path` and `session_id`. Capture real running cockpit/hub UIs against seeded temporary projects and a controlled temporary registry built from public/tracked fixture data—not the user's live registry. Document the exact seed/start/capture commands and verify no auth token, local path, private registry entry, or unreviewed cycle content appears in PNG pixels/adjacent manifest metadata.

2. Reconcile the diagram contract and correct the escalation semantics. The plan promises four README mermaid blocks and four node-matched SVGs, but the proposed README flow names only three diagrams; `tagteam-modes.svg` has no explicit README placement. Map every mermaid block 1:1 to its SVG and README section (or remove the extra diagram consistently). Also replace `Reviewer reviews (≤10 rounds)` and every “round-10 auto-escalation” label with the actual rule: auto-escalation occurs after 10 consecutive stale/no-progress rounds, not at a hard cycle round 10. A progressing cycle may exceed ten total rounds. Make the same wording appear in README, showcase, SVG labels, tests, and the glossary.

3. Separate implementation-review gates from post-approval release operations. The current criteria require a GitHub PR rendering check, PyPI 3.0.0 publication, and an installed upgrade result while also saying “PR at the end.” Publishing cannot sensibly precede implementation approval. Define an in-cycle release-readiness gate (local markdown/mermaid validation, built wheel/sdist metadata, package-tree diff, and a source-installed 0.12.0-project upgrade no-op in a disposable fixture), then a post-approval checklist for PR/merge/tag/PyPI verification. Do not make reviewer approval depend on an already-published artifact.

4. Tighten the showcase-number methodology and drift guard. Define precisely how cycles, rounds, AMENDs/rulings, failed or cancelled usage attempts, duplicate role/round rows, missing token values, and incomplete current cycles are included. Token accounting is provider-specific (the current Claude and Codex rows expose materially different input/cache fields), so only compare like-for-like provider/role series or label the curve as descriptive with that limitation; do not imply a cross-provider efficiency comparison. Add a test that regenerates the marked numbers block and byte-compares it with `docs/showcase.md`, rather than testing arithmetic while relying on findings to notice stale pasted output.

Answers to the open questions: Q1 use PNG captures, with the seeded public fixtures above; Q2 keep the narrow glossary guard after changing it to enforce the accurate stale-round phrase; Q3 keep one `docs/how-tagteam-works.md` file with stable section anchors.

Round 2 — all four points addressed in docs/phases/visual-story-portfolio-feed-30-arc.md (see "Round-2 changes" at the end; open questions resolved per your answers: PNG captures from seeded fixtures, glossary guard kept + stale-round phrase, one HTW file with stable anchors).

1. Public-safe evidence + screenshots. (E) `scripts/showcase_numbers.py export-usage` is a deterministic sanitizer: stdin = `tagteam usage --json`, output `{"schema":"showcase-usage/1","as_of":DATE,"turns":[...]}` with ONLY phase/type/round/role/provider/status/duration_ms/input_tokens/output_tokens/cache_read_tokens/cache_write_tokens/cost_usd — no id/ts/agent/model/exit_code/num_turns/session_id/log_path; sorted + sort_keys → byte-stable. (F) tests: allowed-key schema exactly, no absolute-path-looking string (^/, ^[A-Za-z]:\\, ~/), no session_id/log_path/agent/model/ts key anywhere (recursive), export drops them and is stable across two runs. (C) Screenshots come from `scripts/showcase_seed.py DIR`: three generic projects (demo-api escalated + brief → Needs you; demo-web owed/stale → Waiting; demo-docs approved → Quiet) under a parent named `demo`, synthetic round text authored in the script, seeded usage curve; served with `tagteam serve --theme cockpit --dir DIR/demo-api` and `tagteam hub --registry DIR/registry.json` (never the live registry); 1280×800; public-safety checklist (token is meta-only — DOM text search; no absolute path in pixels — hub rows show name + parent/, path is a title tooltip; no live registry entry; no unreviewed cycle content) recorded item-by-item in findings; PNG test = IHDR 1280×800, no tEXt/iTXt/zTXt chunks, ≤400 KB.

2. Diagram contract 1:1 + escalation semantics. Contract table: ① §2 The loop flowchart ↔ tagteam-loop.svg; ② §5 One cycle stateDiagram-v2 ↔ tagteam-cycle.svg; ③ §6 "Choose how much runs by itself" flowchart (Manual → Watched → Headless) ↔ tagteam-modes.svg; ④ §6 Headless subsection flowchart ↔ tagteam-headless.svg. Every "≤10 rounds"/"round-10" wording removed from the flow, glossary ("auto-escalation after 10 consecutive stale rounds — the lead re-submitting without progress; a progressing cycle may run past round 10"), script (stale-streak metric computed by the cycle._count_stale_rounds rule replaces the round-10 line), SVG labels, and the glossary test (forbids `\b10 rounds\b` / `round[- ]10`; requires "10 consecutive stale rounds" in README).

3. Gates split. "Success criteria — in-cycle gates" are all local: 5-second test on rendered markdown; mermaid rendered locally with mermaid.js in a scratch Chrome page (screenshots in findings) + fence/type/node linter test; SVG conventions + drop-in check in a local copy of aegis.html markup; byte-compare of the numbers block; coverage/link/glossary tests; release-readiness = pytest green, `git diff origin/main -- tagteam/` empty, `pip wheel . --no-deps` METADATA 3.0.0 with tagteam/ file list + hashes equal to the 0.12.0 wheel from PyPI, and source-install `tagteam upgrade` on a 0.12.0-set-up disposable project changing no file. "Post-approval checklist" (PR, CI, GitHub render, tag, PyPI, installed upgrade) is explicitly not a review gate.

4. Methodology + drift guard. Stated in the plan and enforced by the fixture test: cycle = (phase,type), docs/handoffs wins; --as-of DATE pins the data (entries after as-of dropped, later cycles excluded) so the block stays stable while future phases write rounds; outcome from last filtered entry (APPROVE → approved; ESCALATE/NEED_HUMAN → escalated; lead submission/REQUEST_CHANGES → in progress, excluded from rounds-to-approval; aborted); round = lead SUBMIT_FOR_REVIEW; rounds-to-approval = APPROVE's round; AMEND and arbiter rulings ("[ARBITER RULING by" prefix, reviewer role) counted in their own rows, never as rounds/responses, ruling APPROVE closes as "approved (by ruling)"; pushback = REQUEST_CHANGES ÷ SUBMIT_FOR_REVIEW; usage: only status ok in stats, failed/cancelled/timeout counted by outcome, retries → last ok row per (cycle,round,role) + retry count, null tokens excluded and reported "unknown"; curves per (cycle, role, provider) only, labeled descriptive with the provider accounting caveat (Codex input includes cache reads; Claude separate) — no cross-provider claim; cost only where priced. Test byte-compares `report --as-of <block header date> --usage docs/showcase-data/usage-<date>.json` against the marked block in docs/showcase.md.

Also folded in: CITATION.cff (139e099, arbiter) gets version/date bumped with 3.0.0; README license/link-back paragraph kept verbatim in §8.

Round 2 addresses the original review well and is close. Please fix these remaining execution-level blockers.

1. Isolate the upgrade smoke from the real global registry. `tagteam upgrade` has no `--dir` or `--registry` option: it imports `registry.REGISTRY_FILE` (`~/.tagteam/projects.json`), calls the mutating `get_registered_projects()`, then runs setup over every surviving entry. A scratch venv does not isolate that file. As written, the release-readiness recipe can rewrite all real registered projects, not just the disposable fixture. Specify a safe harness that runs the source-installed `upgrade_command()` with both `registry.REGISTRY_DIR` and `registry.REGISTRY_FILE` patched to a temporary registry containing only the disposable project (in a fresh helper process, before the command reads the registry), and checksum the real registry plus every real registered project before/after to prove they were untouched. Do not temporarily replace or edit the real registry. Add a regression test demonstrating an unrelated sentinel project is not visited.

2. Make snapshot pinning and retry order fully specified. `export-usage` currently writes `as_of: DATE` but accepts no date argument, while the raw input contains no top-level capture date. Change the contract to an explicit `export-usage --as-of YYYY-MM-DD`; define DATE as an inclusive UTC calendar day (`ts < next-day 00:00Z`), filter raw turns by that cutoff before stripping `ts`, and apply the identical cutoff semantics to cycle entries in `report`. This makes re-exporting after later turns byte-stable. Because the sanitizer removes both `id` and `ts` but the report chooses the “last” successful duplicate `(cycle, round, role)`, add a safe per-key `attempt` ordinal during export (or another explicit non-sensitive ordering field), include it in the allowed schema/sort key, and test duplicate attempts plus shuffled unrelated rows. Reject a usage file whose embedded `as_of` does not equal the report/block date.

3. Remove the stale-streak off-by-one ambiguity. `_count_stale_rounds` counts equal adjacent submission transitions: 11 identical submissions produce a stale count of 10. The plan currently calls this the “longest run of consecutive lead submissions,” which would normally be 11. Define and report it as consecutive unchanged resubmissions/equal transitions, use the exact production algorithm in the fixture expectation, and make the showcase footnote clear that the first submission starts the baseline and is not itself stale.

Everything else from round 1 is satisfactorily resolved: keep the seeded PNG approach, four-diagram mapping, one-file HTW structure, glossary guard, provider-separated descriptive curves, and post-approval release split.

Round 3 — the three execution-level blockers, in docs/phases/visual-story-portfolio-feed-30-arc.md ("Round-3 changes"; both facts verified against the code: cli.upgrade_command → registry.get_registered_projects (mutating) over module-global REGISTRY_FILE; cycle._count_stale_rounds counts equal adjacent transitions).

1. Upgrade smoke isolated. New `scripts/upgrade_smoke.py --project DIR [--sentinel DIR]`: parent snapshots checksums of the real ~/.tagteam/projects.json (via non-mutating read_registry_raw) and of every framework file setup manages in every real registered project; builds a temp registry dir whose projects.json lists only the disposable project (+ an empty sentinel dir); spawns a fresh helper process (sys.executable -c) with HOME=<tmp> AND tagteam.registry.REGISTRY_DIR/REGISTRY_FILE patched to the temp paths before anything reads the registry, then calls upgrade_command(); parent re-checksums real registry + real projects and fails loudly on any difference; reports the disposable project's before/after diff (must be empty) and that the sentinel was not visited. The real registry is never replaced, edited or copied over. Success criterion 6 now says: only through the harness, never bare `tagteam upgrade`; the 0.12.0 recipe sets HOME for the 0.12.0 `setup` step too. Regression test test_upgrade_smoke_isolated: source-setup disposable + unrelated sentinel → sentinel untouched and not named in helper output, temp registry lists exactly the two dirs, and the real registry file (if present on the machine) byte-identical before/after, checked by the test independently of the harness.

2. Snapshot pinning + retry order specified. `export-usage --as-of YYYY-MM-DD` (required; exit 2 without it); as-of = inclusive UTC calendar day, cutoff ts < DATE+1 00:00:00Z; raw turns filtered by that cutoff BEFORE stripping ts; each surviving turn gets `attempt` = 1..n within (phase,type,round,role) in (ts,id) order; then strip. Schema now phase/type/round/role/attempt/provider/status/duration_ms/input_tokens/output_tokens/cache_read_tokens/cache_write_tokens/cost_usd; sort key (phase,type,round,role,attempt) → byte-identical re-export after later turns. `report` applies the identical cutoff function to cycle entries (legacy entries without ts use the status `date` at 00:00Z), picks the highest-attempt ok row for the curve, and refuses (exit 2) a snapshot whose embedded as_of ≠ its --as-of. Tests: shuffled duplicate attempts + interleaved unrelated rows → ordinals by (ts,id); byte-stable across two runs and with extra post-cutoff turns; boundary (DATE 23:59:59Z in, DATE+1 00:00:00Z out); mismatched as_of → exit 2.

3. Stale streak unambiguous. Defined as consecutive unchanged re-submissions = equal adjacent transitions between successive lead SUBMIT_FOR_REVIEW contents, using a copy of the production loop (first submission is the baseline, never itself stale; 11 identical → 10); fixture expectations are produced by that loop (3 identical + 1 changed → 2; 11 identical → 10); the showcase footnote states the baseline rule in one sentence.

The as-of/attempt contract and stale-transition definition are approved. One blocking contradiction remains in the upgrade harness.

The plan says the temporary `projects.json` lists both the disposable project and an existing empty sentinel directory, then calls the real `upgrade_command()`, while also requiring the sentinel to be unvisited, absent from stdout, and still empty. Production `get_registered_projects()` retains every listed path that is a directory, and `upgrade_command()` calls `setup_main()` for each retained entry. Therefore the listed sentinel will be printed and populated; the proposed regression test cannot pass.

Revise the harness so the temporary registry contains **only** the disposable project. Keep the unrelated sentinel directory outside every registry and assert it remains byte-for-byte/entry-for-entry unchanged and absent from helper output. The temporary-registry assertion must consequently expect exactly one entry, not two.

Also remove every `HOME=<tmp>` override from the recipe and helper. The workspace execution rules prohibit repurposing `HOME`, and it is unnecessary: in each fresh process, import `tagteam.registry`, patch both module globals `REGISTRY_DIR` and `REGISTRY_FILE` to explicit temporary paths, then invoke the relevant 0.12.0 setup function or 3.0 source `upgrade_command()` in that same process. Add a fail-closed assertion immediately before each call that both resolved registry globals are descendants of the expected temporary directory. Snapshot managed destination existence as well as hashes so newly created files in any unrelated path are detected.

With that correction, the plan is ready; no other round-3 changes are requested.

Round 4 — the harness contradiction fixed (docs/phases/visual-story-portfolio-feed-30-arc.md, `scripts/upgrade_smoke.py` paragraph + regression test + "Round-3 changes" item 1 amended):

- Temporary registry lists EXACTLY ONE entry (`--project`); the sentinel is an unrelated dir listed in no registry (real or temporary), and the assertions are: sentinel existence+hash set identical before/after and its path absent from helper stdout; temporary registry still exactly one entry afterwards; real registry bytes identical; every real registered project's managed-destination existence+hash set identical.
- No `HOME` override anywhere (recipe or helper). Each fresh process imports `tagteam.registry`, sets module globals `REGISTRY_DIR` and `REGISTRY_FILE` to explicit temp paths, asserts fail-closed immediately before the call that both resolved globals are descendants of the expected temp dir (`resolve()` + `is_relative_to`), then calls `upgrade_command()` — and the 0.12.0 `setup` step in the release recipe is run the same way from the 0.12.0 venv (patch its registry globals, same assertion, call its setup function) so 0.12.0's own registry write lands in the scratch registry.
- Snapshots record existence AND sha256 for every managed destination (from tagteam.setup's framework file list) in every real registered project, the disposable project and the sentinel, so a newly created file in an unrelated path is detected, not just a changed one.
- Regression test: source-setup disposable (registry globals monkeypatched in-process) + a sentinel dir containing one file; sentinel unchanged and unnamed; temp registry == one entry; real registry byte-identical if present (checked by the test independently of the harness).

No other changes.

The round-4 harness correction is approved. One final unsafe bypass remains at the post-approval call site.

The post-approval checklist still says: install 3.0.0 in a scratch venv, then run `tagteam upgrade` on the 0.12.0-set-up project. A scratch venv does not isolate `~/.tagteam/projects.json`; that bare installed command can still prune the real registry and rewrite every real registered project, exactly the hazard the harness now prevents.

Change the post-approval installed-wheel verification to use the same isolated mechanism: invoke `scripts/upgrade_smoke.py` with the **3.0.0 venv's Python interpreter** (so the helper imports the published wheel), an explicit temporary registry containing only the disposable 0.12.0 project, the fail-closed registry-global assertions, and the unrelated sentinel/real-registry/managed-destination before-after checks. State explicitly that bare `tagteam upgrade` is forbidden in both the in-cycle and post-approval recipes. Add a test/argument contract proving the harness can select an explicit target interpreter and that the helper reports the imported `tagteam` version/path, so the post-release check cannot accidentally exercise the source checkout.

No other changes are requested; after removing this last bypass, approve.

Round 5 — the last bypass removed (docs/phases/visual-story-portfolio-feed-30-arc.md: harness paragraph, post-approval checklist, regression tests, "Round-5 change"):

- Post-approval installed-wheel verification runs ONLY through `scripts/upgrade_smoke.py --python <3.0.0 scratch venv python> --expect-version 3.0.0 --project <0.12.0-set-up disposable> --sentinel <unrelated dir>`: the helper process is the selected interpreter, prints the imported tagteam.__version__ and __file__ before anything else, and the parent refuses (exit 2) unless the version matches --expect-version and the path is under that interpreter's sys.prefix — so the check cannot accidentally exercise the source checkout. Same temporary registry (only the disposable project), same fail-closed registry-global assertions before the call, same sentinel / real-registry / managed-destination existence+hash before/after checks as the in-cycle gate.
- Stated explicitly for both recipes: bare `tagteam upgrade` is forbidden; the harness is the only permitted way to run an upgrade in this phase.
- Argument/test contract: `--python EXE` (default sys.executable) + `--expect-version`; tests (a) `--python sys.executable` echoes the source checkout's version and tagteam/__init__.py path, (b) `--python` pointing at a shim that reports a different version/path with `--expect-version 3.0.0` → exit 2 naming the mismatch.

No other changes.
